page: Hetzner Cloud ccx13 is an entry-tier general purpose virtual server configured with dedicated compute resources. Operating on the QEMU hypervisor with the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 2 vCPUs across 1 physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AES, and SHA-NI while omitting AVX-512 extensions. The server is allocated 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.91 GB per vCPU, and integrates 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations show a distinct contrast between single-core throughput and multi-threaded scaling. The instance achieves strong results in single-threaded tests, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1940.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3074.79, placing it in the upper quartile of tested systems. However, constrained by its single physical core allocation, overall multi-core throughput lands in the bottom 25%, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2469.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3850.73. Memory performance metrics reflect moderate uncached write bandwidth of 26.66 GB/sec alongside lower cached throughput and memory subsystem ratings.

Because compute capacity is fully dedicated rather than shared or burstable, the ccx13 maintains consistent execution times free from noisy-neighbor CPU throttling. Its limited parallel core count and memory bandwidth restrict high-throughput database workloads and heavy concurrent traffic, reflected in a PassMark database score of 989.94 and static web serving rate of 3.1 GB/sec. Consequently, the instance is tailored for predictable single-thread-intensive processes, lightweight background workers, low-concurrency API backends, and modular microservices requiring dedicated hardware reliability.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx13 is a dedicated general purpose virtual instance powered by AMD EPYC x86_64 processors on a QEMU hypervisor. The instance provisions 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core and 2 threads running at 2.0 GHz, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache, 8.0 GB of RAM, and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark results illustrate strong single-core capabilities, registering a 1940.0 Geekbench single-core score and 3074.79 in stress-ng. However, aggregate multi-core throughput and memory subsystem metrics rank lower due to the 2-vCPU constraint, illustrated by a 2469.0 Geekbench multi-core mark and 3.1 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Delivering predictable dedicated compute without thread contention, the ccx13 serves workloads such as lightweight application services, low-concurrency API backends, development environments, and single-threaded automation pipelines requiring stable baseline execution.
